title: The affine line and the punctured line over a base
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme,
and use the affine-line datum of [def-pur-affine-line-datum]: the
projection $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$, the zero section $s$, the open
complement $j:\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$, the composite
$\pi=pj:\mathbf G_{m,Y}\to Y$, the finite-level twist
$\Lambda(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$, and the Kummer class
$\kappa(t)\in H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\Lambda(1))$ of the coordinate. Write
$R^m\pi_*=\mathcal H^m R\pi_*$ for the cohomology sheaves of
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then:

1. *(Acyclicity of the affine line.)* The units
$\Lambda_Y\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}$ and
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)$ are isomorphisms; so
$R^mp_*\Lambda(1)=0$ for $m>0$.
1. *(The Kummer generator.)* The unit
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to R^0\pi_*\Lambda(1)$ — equivalently, restriction along $j$
composed with the pullback $p^*$ — is an isomorphism, and the map
$$
\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1),\qquad 1\longmapsto\kappa(t),
$$
sending $1$ to the image of $\kappa(t)$ under the edge map
$H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\Lambda(1))=H^1(Y,R\pi_*\Lambda(1))\to
\Gamma(Y,R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1))$, is an isomorphism: $R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)$
is free of rank one on $\kappa(t)$.
1. *(Vanishing above degree one.)* $R^m\pi_*\Lambda(1)=0$ for $m\geq2$.
1. *(Base change.)* For every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$ of separated
finite-type $k$-schemes, with base changes
$p':\mathbf A^1_{Y'}\to Y'$, $\pi':\mathbf G_{m,Y'}\to Y'$ and
$g':\mathbf G_{m,Y'}\to\mathbf G_{m,Y}$, the pullback of the Kummer class
is the Kummer class, $g'^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t')$, and the base-change
morphisms
$$
g^*Rp_*\Lambda(1)\to Rp'_*\Lambda(1),\qquad
g^*R\pi_*\Lambda(1)\to R\pi'_*\Lambda(1)
$$
are isomorphisms.

The same base-change conclusion also holds for $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point, without requiring $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ to be of finite type over $k$. Thus (1)–(3) can be checked on geometric fibres: over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ the affine line has only constant $H^0$, while the punctured line has constant $H^0$, $H^1$ freely generated by $\kappa(t)$, and no higher cohomology.

proof.text: Put $r=\ell^N$. The affine-line datum already assumes $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, so $N=n/e\geq1$, $rA=0$, and $A$ is finite free over $\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$ by [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]. Since $\ell\neq p=\operatorname{char}k$, $r$ is invertible in every $k$-scheme; no condition on whether $p$ divides the exponent $N$ is needed. Choose a primitive $r$-th root $\zeta\in k$ by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. For any $k$-scheme $T$, the factorization $X^r-1=\prod_{a\in\mathbf Z/r}(X-\zeta^a)$ has pairwise invertible differences. Thus the roots-of-unity scheme is the disjoint union of $r$ copies of $T$, and $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ identifies the constant $\mathbf Z/r$-sheaf with $\mu_{r,T}$. Tensoring this map with $A$ identifies $A_T$ with $A(1)_T$. These identifications commute with every $k$-morphism because the same roots and the same polynomial factorization pull back. In particular all the twisted coefficient sheaves in the question are inverse images from the base, and the order of their underlying finite abelian group is a power of $\ell$.

source.place: Proof, opening paragraph: finite twist and primitive-root trivialization

proof.text: The computations below may be made with underlying abelian etale sheaves. [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of each module-valued higher direct image with the corresponding abelian higher direct image, including degrees zero and negative degrees. [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] supplies the natural module/abelian comparison on global cohomology, also applied to each etale test scheme. The comparisons can be computed with resolutions: an injective module sheaf has acyclic underlying abelian sheaf for global sections by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-injective-forget-acyclic], and [src-right-derived-functor-plus-acyclic-unit] computes the derived functor on such a resolution. [lem-sc-acyclic-comparison-natural] shows that applying a map of resolutions gives the same cohomology map under this comparison. Consequently constants, coefficient maps, and the resolution maps used below keep their actual maps on cohomology after forgetting scalars. All maps considered are $A$-linear; a bijective underlying homomorphism of $A$-modules has an $A$-linear inverse (if $f(x)=y$, then $f(ax)=ay$). In particular [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients](1)–(3) identifies the underlying module-derived exchange with the specified abelian-derived exchange, under its canonical inverse-image and direct-image comparisons; it also reflects invertibility. Thus using an abelian exchange calculation below proves a statement about the actual module exchange, not only about its source and target.

source.place: Proof, opening paragraph: compute finite-torsion cohomology on the small etale site

proof.text: Here is the naturality of the Kummer class that will be used at each restriction. For any morphism $u:T'\to T$ of $k$-schemes, pull back the exact Kummer sequence $0\to\mu_{r,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T}\xrightarrow{r}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to0$ of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Pullback of units defines maps from both $u^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}$ terms to $\mathbf G_{m,T'}$; their restriction on the kernels is the canonical identification $u^{-1}\mu_{r,T}=\mu_{r,T'}$ from step 1. They commute with the power maps because $u^*(v^r)=(u^*v)^r$, giving a morphism to the Kummer sequence on $T'$. [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback](3) commutes the boundary with inverse image, and [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor](1) commutes it with this morphism of short exact sequences. Therefore $u^*\delta_T(v)=\delta_{T'}(u^*v)$. The coefficient map $\mu_r\to\mu_r\otimes A$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, also commutes with inverse image, so the equality holds with $A(1)$-coefficients. Applied to the coordinate, it gives $u^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(u^*t)$.

source.place: Proof, Step 2 Kummer restriction and Step 3 Kummer base change

proof.text: Compute over $k$ first, for $C=\mathbf A^1_k$ or $\mathbf G_{m,k}$. These are smooth separated connected affine curves. Use the exact Kummer sequence with exponent $r$ from [lem-sc-kummer-exact]. The long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact], together with [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic], identifies $H^1(C,\mu_r)$ with the cokernel of the $r$-power map on units, since [lem-pur-affine-punctured-line-algebra] gives $\operatorname{Pic}(C)=0$. For the line the units are $k^\times$, and this power map is surjective because $k$ is algebraically closed. For the punctured line the units are $k^\times t^{\mathbf Z}$; modulo $r$-th powers their quotient is $\mathbf Z/r$, whose class of $t$ maps to $\delta(t)$. Thus $H^1(\mathbf A^1_k,\mu_r)=0$ and $H^1(\mathbf G_{m,k},\mu_r)=\mathbf Z/r$ with the specified Kummer generator. This proves the generator statement rather than merely the existence of an abstract rank-one group.

source.place: Unit proof, Degrees 0 and 1; replaces the invocation of thm-pur-kummer-affine-line by its Kummer calculation

proof.text: On each curve the constant-section map computes $H^0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected]; step 1 therefore identifies $H^0(C,\mu_r)$ with $\mu_r(k)$ via constants, and restriction from the line to the punctured line preserves this identification. Apply [thm-sc-affine-cohomology] with its integer $n=r$ (not $n=N$): $r$ is prime to $p$ and both curves are affine, so the constant $\mathbf Z/r$-sheaf has zero cohomology in degrees $q>1$. The primitive-root identification in step 1 gives the same vanishing for $\mu_r$. Now [lem-pur-kummer-coefficient-base-change] applies, since $A$ is finite free over $\mathbf Z/r$ by step 1. It tensors the preceding computations with $A$, preserving the Kummer boundary. We obtain constants in degree zero, zero positive cohomology for the line, and $A\kappa(t)$ in degree one and zero in degrees $q\geq2$ for the punctured line. Negative cohomology is zero for sheaves placed in degree zero. These computations are the flat-coefficient alternative expressly allowed at the end of the unit's Coefficients paragraph.

source.place: Unit proof, Coefficients (last parenthesis), Clause (c), and Degrees 0 and 1

proof.text: Perform the relative calculation for any $k$-scheme $B$, using $C_B=C_k\times_k B$ and $a_B:C_B\to B$, with $C_k$ either of the two curves in steps 4–5. In particular this includes $B=Y$, $Y'$, and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for a geometric point. For a geometric point $\bar b$ of $B$, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{B,\bar b}$. The map $a_B$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its base change to $S$ is $C_S$. The canonical stalk formula [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] identifies $(R^q(a_B)_*A(1))_{\bar b}$ with $H^q(C_S,A(1))$. To track the actual sections, use [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf]: a global class restricts on an etale neighbourhood $U$ to its class on $C_U$, then gives a section of the sheafification. Its germ maps in the canonical stalk formula to the restriction of the same class on $C_S$. Thus the unit gives constants and the germ of the edge section of $\kappa(t)$ gives $\kappa(t)|_{C_S}$. This follows by sending the class to each etale neighbourhood and then to its limit, not by assuming arbitrary base change for $a_B$.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: strict-henselization stalk formula and compatibility with constants and classes

proof.text: In the square $C_S=C_k\times_k S$, write $f:C_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g:S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $h:C_S\to C_k$, and $e:C_S\to S$. Here $f$ is smooth and $g$ is affine (both $S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are affine), so $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; $S$ need not be of finite type over $k$. The sheaf $A(1)_S$ is constant by step 1 and has order invertible on $k$. Hence [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] gives the canonical isomorphisms $f^{-1}R^qg_*A(1)\to R^qh_*A(1)$. By [sbc-lem-strict-henselian-constant-cohomology], $H^q(S,A(1))$ consists of constants in degree zero and is zero otherwise. For any geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, its strict henselization is $\operatorname{Spec}k$ itself, since $k$ has no proper finite separable extension. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] applied to the affine map $g$ computes each geometric stalk of $R^qg_*A(1)$ as $H^q(S,A(1))$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], the degree-zero unit identifies $A(1)_k$ with $g_*A(1)$ and the higher sheaves are zero. Thus $R^qh_*A(1)=0$ for $q>0$, and in degree zero the base-change map identifies constants with $h_*A(1)$. The degree-zero map is the usual adjunction map by the degree-zero clause of [sbc-def-base-change-map]; evaluated on a constant section $a$ it is the constant section $a$ on $C_S$. Consequently the unit $A(1)_{C_k}\to Rh_*A(1)_{C_S}$ is an isomorphism on all cohomology sheaves, hence an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. Smooth base change is applied with the smooth arrow $C_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, not with $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Unit proof, Reduction to a geometric fibre: the rotated smooth-base-change square

proof.text: Apply derived global sections on $C_k$ to the unit isomorphism of step 7. [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition](5) identifies $R\Gamma(C_k,Rh_*A(1))$ with $R\Gamma(C_S,A(1))$. More precisely [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](1),(2) says that this identification after $R\Gamma$ of the unit is the actual pullback $h^*$. Hence $h^*:H^q(C_k,A(1))\to H^q(C_S,A(1))$ is an isomorphism in every degree. It carries constants to constants; for the punctured line step 3 gives $h^*\kappa(t_k)=\kappa(t_S)$ because the coordinate pulls back to the coordinate. The map $C_S\to C_B$ also pulls the coordinate to $t_S$, so step 3 identifies the germ of the relative Kummer section in step 6 with this same generator. There is no assertion here that a stalk of an arbitrary direct image is the cohomology of a geometric fibre.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: composition and identification of pullback of the Kummer generator

proof.text: Combining steps 5–8 computes the stalks of every $R^q(a_B)_*A(1)$. For the line they are constants in degree zero and zero otherwise; for the punctured line they are constants in degree zero, $A\kappa(t_S)$ in degree one, and zero otherwise. [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] therefore proves that the degree-zero unit is an isomorphism, that the sheaf map $A_B\to R^1\pi_*A(1)$ determined by the edge section $\kappa(t)$ is an isomorphism, and that all asserted higher sheaves vanish. Forgetting a module structure detects isomorphisms by the elementary inverse calculation in step 2. For the line, [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] promotes the cohomology calculation of the unit to $A(1)_B\simeq Rp_*A(1)$. The same primitive-root trivialization of step 1 identifies the untwisted unit with this unit, proving untwisted acyclicity too. Restriction along $j$ takes the pulled-back constant $a$ on $\mathbf A^1_B$ to the pulled-back constant $a$ on $\mathbf G_{m,B}$, so its composite with $p^*$ is exactly the degree-zero unit described above. This proves clauses (1)–(3), including identification of the specified maps.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1–2: conclude the units, generator, and vanishing by geometric stalks

proof.text: Let $g:B'\to B$ be any $k$-morphism under consideration, and let $a':C_{B'}\to B'$ and $v:C_{B'}\to C_B$ be its base-change square for $a=a_B$. With constant coefficients, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies pullback with exact inverse image. The exchange $b:g^*Ra_*\to Ra'_*v^*$ is the mate defined in [sbc-def-base-change-map]. For an object $L$ on $B$, its composite with $g^*\eta_a(L)$ is $\eta_{a'}(g^*L)$ after identifying $v^*a^*=a'^*g^*$. Indeed, transposing under $a'^*\dashv Ra'_*$ turns this composite into $v^*\varepsilon_a\circ v^*a^*\eta_a$, which is the identity by the triangle identity, while the transpose of $\eta_{a'}$ is also the identity. Thus in degree zero the exchange preserves exactly the constants used to identify both sides in step 9, and is an isomorphism in that degree.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: the mate and the unit compatibility, with the triangle-identity calculation

proof.text: For degree one, first forget coefficients using the specified exchange equality of step 2. [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology] identifies the cohomology of the abelian derived exchange with the map obtained by applying underived exchange termwise to a resolution $F\to I^\bullet$, comparing $v^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ with a resolution on $C_{B'}$, and taking cohomology. The representative-section formula of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] sends a section on $C_U$ to its restriction on $C_{U\times_B B'}$. For etale $U\to B$, the projections $C_U\to C_B$ and $C_{U\times_B B′}\to C_{B′}$ are etale; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] with constant ring $\mathbf Z$ makes the restrictions of the chosen injective resolutions injective, so their section complexes compute the local cohomology in the presheaf. Accordingly a cocycle in $I^q(C_U)$ maps to that restricted cocycle followed by the resolution comparison to $J^\bullet$. This is exactly the pullback recipe in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Passing to cohomology classes and then to the associated sheaves of [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf] shows that exchange sends the pulled-back edge section of a global class to the edge section of its pullback. For $\kappa(t)$, step 3 identifies this pullback with $\kappa(t')$ because $v^*t=t'$. The coefficient comparison in step 2 makes this the same equality for the module-derived exchange. Both degree-one sheaves for $\mathbf G_m$ are freely generated by these sections by step 9, so this degree-one exchange is an isomorphism. For the affine line both degree-one sheaves are zero.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: compatibility with classes, written on cocycles rather than asserted

proof.text: The pullback is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies the cohomology of $g^*Ra_*A(1)$ with $g^*R^qa_*A(1)$. By step 9, all cohomology outside degree zero (for the line), respectively degrees zero and one (for the punctured line), is zero on both sides. Steps 10–11 give isomorphisms in each remaining degree. [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] now makes each exchange an isomorphism. Step 3 already proves $v^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t')$. This proves clause (4). Steps 6–11 used no finite-type hypothesis on $B'$: for $B'=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ the same calculation applies, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed and $C_{B'}$ still affine of dimension one over $\Omega$. Thus the additional geometric-point case holds even when $\Omega$ is not finite over $k$, and the canonical fibre comparisons identify all the constants and Kummer generators just computed.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: conclude exchange is invertible, and justify the geometric-point case

proof.text: Pass to the small pro-etale site. For $a=p$ or $\pi$, the morphism $a:C_B\to B$ is affine, hence qcqs, and remains so after every base change, including a geometric point. The finite coefficient sheaves in degree zero are in $D^+$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] and use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] to choose its specified invertible counit mate $b_a$. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1)–(3), comparison identifies constant coefficients, is exact, and commutes with cohomology sheaves. Thus the vanishing calculations of step 9 hold on the pro-etale site as well. [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] supplies the bounded-below fully faithful comparison.

source.place: Proof, opening paragraph: qcqs direct-image comparison and cohomology sheaves

proof.text:
The named comparison preserves the units by [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility]. In its notation take $L_1=a_{\mathrm{et}}^*$, $R_1=Ra_{\mathrm{et},*}$, $L_2=a_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$, $R_2=Ra_{\mathrm{proet},*}$, $G=
u_B^*$, $H=
u_{C_B}^*$, and $\alpha$ the inverse of the specified pullback comparison. Its right mate is precisely $b_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The leaf's identity says that $b_{a,a^*L}\circ
u_B^*\eta_a^e(L)=Ra_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\alpha_L)\circ\eta_a^p(
u_B^*L)$. Identifying coefficients through $\alpha_L$ makes this the pro-etale unit. Hence step 9 gives the stated affine-line acyclicity units and the punctured-line degree-zero unit, with their actual maps.

source.place: Proof, opening paragraph: transport the units, using the Mathlib mate-unit identity

proof.text:
Write $T=\mathbf G_{m,B}$ and $F=A(1)^{\mathrm{et}}_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], $c^1_{T,F}$ is $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},\eta_F)$ followed by the final-object comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-sections-pushforward]. Unwind it on an injective module resolution $F	o I^ ullet$ and an injective resolution $
u_T^*I^ ullet	o J^ ullet$ of $
u_T^*F$ (exactness of $
u_T^*$, [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](2)): $
u_{T,*}J^ ullet$ computes $R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*F$, the composite $I^ ullet	o
u_{T,*}
u_T^*I^ ullet	o
u_{T,*}J^ ullet$ lifts the unit, and evaluation at the final object gives $\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},I^ ullet)	o\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{proet}},
u_T^*I^ ullet)	o\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{proet}},J^ ullet)$: pull back the cocycle, then compare with the resolution. This is the recipe of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] for $
u_T$ at the final object, formed with module resolutions, i.e. the canonical global-cohomology pullback; [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] says that forgetting scalars carries it to the abelian canonical pullback, which is the isomorphism of [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] used in [def-pur-affine-line-datum] to define $\kappa(t)$ as the image of $\kappa_{\mathrm{et}}(t)$, under the datum's identification of $
u_T^{-1}A(1)^{\mathrm{et}}_T$ with $A(1)_T$. Hence $c^1_{T,F}(\kappa_{\mathrm{et}}(t))=\kappa(t)$. Apply [lem-pur-site-comparison-edge-section] with $u=\pi$, $F$ and $q=1$. Its equality identifies the pulled-back edge section of $\kappa_{\mathrm{et}}(t)$ under $\mathcal H^1(b_\pi)$ with the edge section of $\kappa(t)$. Consequently the image of the isomorphism $A_B	o R^1\pi_{\mathrm{et},*}A(1)$ in step 9 is exactly the asserted map $1\mapsto\kappa(t)$ on the pro-etale site. Exact comparison preserves its invertibility. This settles the specified generator, as well as the cohomology groups on geometric fibres.

source.place: Proof, opening paragraph: transport the Kummer class (the datum's canonical comparison) and its edge section

proof.text: For each square in step 12, [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] gives $T\circ\nu_{B'}^*(\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{et}})=\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{proet}}\circ S$, with the specified invertible pullback/direct-image comparisons $S,T$. Its qcqs assumptions concern $a$ and $a'$, already checked in step 13; they hold even when $B'=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is not finite type over $k$. Since step 12 proves that the etale exchange is invertible, its image under comparison is invertible, and conjugating by $S,T$ proves that the specified pro-etale exchange is invertible. Thus the base-change isomorphisms of step 12 are the stated pro-etale exchange maps. Together with the compared classes of step 15, this completes the transport of all clauses to the statement's site convention.
